description: Agent Bookkeeping: submit the accounts receivable ledger with the ledger balance it should total to: the receivables report with its reference, the day it is read on, its currency, each customer invoice with its id, customer, invoice number, invoice date, due date, amount and the amount paid, each aging bucket as stated (current, 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 or over 90 days) with its total, each customer payment with its customer, reference, amount and the amount applied, and each customer record with its name; the ledger with its date, currency and accounts receivable balance. The signed report gives the receivables report and the books, each stated aging bucket recomputed from the open invoices, the open invoices less unapplied payments totalled against the ledger balance, each customer payment left unapplied, each customer recorded more than once, and each invoice long past due, and counts them, and names a divergent receivables ledger: aging buckets unlike the open invoices, a receivables total unlike the ledger’s accounts receivable balance, a customer payment never applied, and duplicate customer records; then a stale invoice more than ninety days past due and another currency, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No invoices, no aging buckets, no due dates or report date, no ledger balance, or no customer records leaves those points unverified. Invoices age in whole days from their due date, amounts compare to the cent in one currency, and customers read as parties without case, punctuation or a legal suffix. This checks the receivables ledger itself: wever_invoice-aging-brief briefs the aging of open invoices and wever_invoice-payment-match matches one payment to one invoice, while the receivables check reads every invoice, payment and customer record together against the ledger balance. Verdict bookkeeping_receivables_divergent, bookkeeping_receivables_partial, bookkeeping_receivables_unverified or bookkeeping_receivables_consistent. POST /api/bookkeeping-receivables-check. Reads the bookkeeping records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the books as supplied only: it never posts or edits an entry, never moves money or pays a bill, never files anything with any authority and gives no tax advice, which stay with the business, its bookkeeper and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Bookkeeping reads a business’s own books for internal consistency and against the records they should agree with: a general-ledger extract, a bank reconciliation, journal entries, a chart of accounts, a period close, the accounts payable ledger, a payroll register and the accounts receivable ledger, each against its own debits and credits, the source totals supplied, the bank statement and the ledger balance, the open period, the posting queue and recurring entries, or the ledger postings and pay schedule it should agree with. The family reads bookkeeping, the record a business keeps of its own transactions in its ledger and journals, and reads the records against each other. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-bookkeeping-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-bookkeeping/.
